title: Marvell Stock (MRVL) Falls 13.2% on Reports of Lumentum Deal (Oct 29)
summary: Marvell stock (MRVL) fell 13.24% to $218.34 on Oct. 29 after reports that the chipmaker is in advanced talks to buy optical maker Lumentum.
body_markdown:
Even after the slide, Marvell stays 208.87% above its 52-week low, while it now sits 33.81% below its 52-week high.


## Why Marvell Stock Fell


Financial media tied the drop to a Bloomberg report that Marvell is in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum, a maker of lasers and high-speed optical components used in AI data centers. The report first moved both stocks in after-hours trading on Wednesday, October 28, per[24/7 Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/marvell-talks-buy-83-billion-130754067.html) , which said Bloomberg valued Lumentum at about $83 billion and Marvell at roughly $221 billion. Thursday was the first full session to absorb the news.


On Thursday, October 29, Investopedia reported that an announcement is possible as early as next week and that neither Marvell nor Lumentum responded to its requests for comment. According to[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-oct-29-214330390.html) , the deal is said to be an all-stock transaction, a final agreement has not yet been officially reached, and investors focused on financing and dilution risk.


No company release or filing on the talks was available at publication. Per 24/7 Wall St., neither company has confirmed the talks or filed an 8-K, and nothing has been signed.


## MRVL Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Marvell already buys lasers from Lumentum, and Investopedia noted that a deal would give it more direct access to a major supplier, while Lumentum's CEO said earlier this month that its optical networking capacity is sold out through early 2029.
- Marvell recently raised its long-term sales targets on data center demand, according to Investopedia, and Motley Fool reported that its October 6 investor day lifted the fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to $20 billion.
- Nvidia made $2 billion investments in both Marvell and Lumentum earlier this year, per Investopedia.


### Risks


- The talks remain unconfirmed: nothing has been signed and no price, premium or cash-and-stock mix has been disclosed, per 24/7 Wall St., which added that a takeover would normally add a premium to Lumentum's value.
- Marvell held about $3.92 billion in cash at quarter-end, so a deal would need stock, debt or both, according to 24/7 Wall St., keeping the financing and dilution concerns Motley Fool described in focus.
- Marvell fell more than its chip peers and the Nasdaq in the same session, showing how sharply the stock reacted to deal uncertainty.
